Odin 🍽️ — a Signal bot for the weekly open Sunday dinner.

```
odin [--version] <command> [options]
```

## Global options

| Option | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--version` | – | show program's version number and exit |

## Environment

Configured by env vars: SIGNAL_NUMBER, SIGNAL_API_URL, ODIN_CONFIG, ODIN_DB, ODIN_LOG_LEVEL, ODIN_HEALTH_PORT. The group IDs are stored in the database by odin setup; FLAT_GROUP_ID and DINNER_GROUP_ID optionally override them.

## `odin run`

Run the bot until SIGTERM or SIGINT; waits while ODIN is not set up.

```
odin run
```

No options.

## `odin setup`

Interactive setup: register the number, set PIN and profile, choose the groups; resumes where it stopped.

```
odin setup [--status] [--pin] [--redo STEP]
```

| Option | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--status` | – | only show which steps are done, change nothing; exit code 0 when fully set up |
| `--pin` | – | enter an own PIN instead of a generated one; also sets a new PIN if one is set |
| `--redo` | `STEP` (`pin`, `hello`, `groups`, `test`) | repeat a finished step (pin, hello, groups, test); can be given several times |

## `odin list-groups`

Print the Signal groups the bot is in, with their IDs (for debugging, or for the FLAT_GROUP_ID / DINNER_GROUP_ID overrides); needs only SIGNAL_NUMBER and SIGNAL_API_URL.

```
odin list-groups
```

No options.

## `odin check-config`

Validate the config file and env vars and print the next scheduled actions.

```
odin check-config
```

No options.

## `odin health`

Ask the running bot whether it is healthy (GET /health on ODIN_HEALTH_PORT); exit code 0 when it is up, 1 when it is down or does not answer.

```
odin health [--setup-ok]
```

| Option | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--setup-ok` | – | also exit with 0 while ODIN only waits for odin setup (the container health check, so that a first start before odin setup counts as started) |
